title.en: Two killers, half a dose each

subtitle.zh-TW: 兩份毒各自都毒不死市長，合起來才致命，兩名殺手都是原因。
subtitle.en: Neither dose alone would kill the mayor; together they do, and both are causes.

story.zh-TW: 考慮市長的咖啡被下毒的情境。毒藥的致死劑量是 10 毫克，甲下了 5 毫克，乙也下了 5 毫克。市長喝下咖啡後中毒身亡。
story.en: Consider two killers who each put poison in the mayor's coffee. The lethal dose is 10 milligrams; the first adds 5 milligrams and the second adds 5 milligrams as well. The mayor drinks the coffee and dies of poisoning.

zh-TW.sentence: 毒藥的致死劑量是 10 毫克，甲下了 5 毫克，乙也下了 5 毫克。
市長喝下咖啡後中毒身亡。

en.sentence: the first adds 5 milligrams and the second adds 5 milligrams as well.
The mayor drinks the coffee and dies of poisoning.

text.zh-TW: 兩人都下了毒。缺了任何一份，市長都不會死，所以兩名殺手都是死因。
text.en: Both put poison in the coffee and without either dose the mayor would not have died, so both killers are causes of his death.

explanation.zh-TW: 模型取自王一奇與王鵬翔 (2021) 的 HD：A 表示甲下半分毒，B 表示乙下半分毒，D 表示市長死亡，D = A·B。兩份毒缺一不可，各定義都判兩人是原因。一個反事實依賴（counterfactual dependence）要靠另一個異常事件才成立時，Hitchcock (2007) 稱它為寄生的（parasitic），並以網絡不自足來刻畫。在 HD 裡，A 取預設值（default value）0 時，D 也取預設值 0，網絡是自足的。A 對 D 的依賴卻要靠 B 這個異常事件。所以網絡自足與否，區分不了寄生的依賴。
explanation.en: The model is the HD of Wang and Wang (2021): A = 1 (the first killer adds half a dose), B = 1 (the second does), D = A·B (the mayor dies), with the same structure as the doctor case they discuss. Neither half-dose can be dropped, so each killer is a counterfactual cause and the definitions agree. The case has another purpose: Hitchcock (2007) calls a counterfactual dependence that rests on some other abnormal event parasitic and characterises it by a network that is not self-contained. In HD the network linking A and D is self-contained (when A takes its default value 0, D also takes its default 0), so A is a typical cause; yet A's counterfactual dependence holds only because of B, a deviant event. Whether the network is self-contained and whether the dependence is parasitic therefore do not correspond, and self-containment cannot be used to tell the parasitic from the rest.

sources.citation: Wang, P.-H., & Wang, L. (2021). Parasitic counterfactual dependence and paradigmatic causation [in Chinese]. Philosophical Journal (National Chengchi University), 45, 39–90.

verdicts.note: Witness: A = 0 with B = 1 held, a world no more deviant than the actual one.
